answer: Sybil resistance rests on a priced identity anchor, not on counting accounts. Each participant posts a bond locked while their identity is active, and the protocol records one canonical identity per bond. N identities need N locked bonds plus distinct audit work, so the thousandth fake account costs as much as the first. Withdrawing a bond to clone forfeits accumulated history. Honest miners reach the summit through one account and steady work; a coalition pays full price per clone, so its payoff shrinks while cost stays flat. The crystal point: duplicates earn nothing; the meadow stays calm.
